=== SHEET: Delimitación del dominio ===
Delimitación del dominio de conocimiento — Document Set (Tarea 1)
Alcance temático | El Document Set (31 artículos) cubre la programación (scheduling) y optimización energética en entornos industriales de fabricación de acero, con foco en: programación de hornos de recalentamiento (reheating/heating furnace), laminación en caliente (hot rolling/hot strip mill), colada continua/aceración (steelmaking-continuous casting), despacho de cucharas (ladle dispatching/scheduling), y tratamiento térmico (heat treatment).
Subtemas identificados | (1) Modelos matemáticos y metaheurísticas de programación (MILP, matheurísticas, algoritmos genéticos, grey wolf optimizer, NSGA-II); (2) Aprendizaje por refuerzo profundo (DRL) y multiagente aplicado a programación y gestión energética; (3) Gemelos digitales (Digital Twin) para monitorización y control de procesos; (4) Inteligencia artificial explicable (XAI) aplicada a algoritmos de programación/optimización; (5) Eficiencia energética y programación 'verde' (green scheduling); (6) Incertidumbre y robustez en la programación dinámica.
Tipos de fuente | Artículos de revista (Elsevier: Computers & Industrial Engineering, Applied Energy, Expert Systems With Applications, Journal of Cleaner Production, Computers in Industry, etc.), IEEE Transactions (Industrial Electronics, Industrial Informatics, Cybernetics), revistas MDPI (Machines, Sustainability, J. of Manufacturing and Materials Processing), y actas de congresos (IFAC, CCDC, CPSL, IHIET, J. Phys. Conf. Series).
Rango temporal | 2016 – 2026 (predominan publicaciones de 2019 en adelante; varios artículos son muy recientes, de 2025-2026).
Vacíos / limitaciones detectadas | Varios PDFs no incluyen metadatos de autor u palabras clave embebidos (se completaron manualmente a partir del texto). Algunos artículos no declaran keywords explícitas (marcados como N/D en el inventario). No se detectaron documentos escaneados (todos tienen capa de texto extraíble).
Herramientas usadas para el escaneo | poppler-utils (pdfinfo, pdftotext) para inspección y extracción de metadatos/texto; extracción manual de metadatos faltantes desde el texto de la primera página; openpyxl/pandas para construir el inventario en Excel.

Task 2: Topographical Mapping
Document Analysis and Organizational Synthesis — Industrial AI for Steel Production Scheduling
Objetivo
Construir un mapa del conocimiento contenido en el Document Set (31 artículos), identificando dónde se concentra el conocimiento y dónde está aislado, mediante dos entregables: un árbol jerárquico de temas y un grafo de red de referencias cruzadas.

2. Grafo de red de referencias cruzadas (Cross-Reference Network Graph)
El siguiente grafo representa los mismos 4 clústeres y 9 subtemas como nodos centrales, con los 31 documentos conectados a su(s) subtema(s) asignado(s). Las líneas rojas discontinuas marcan relaciones cruzadas ocultas: subtemas que no son adyacentes en la jerarquía pero que comparten documentos, revelando puentes temáticos (p. ej., entre 'Energy-Efficient Scheduling' y 'Deep Reinforcement Learning' a través de los documentos que aplican DRL a la optimización energética).
Lectura de las relaciones cruzadas identificadas
• A2 (Energy-Efficient Scheduling) ↔ A1 (Deterministic/Robust Scheduling): comparten P1, P16, P26 — muchos modelos deterministas ya incorporan el objetivo energético.
• A2 ↔ B1 (Deep RL): comparten P5 — la optimización energética empieza a resolverse con DRL, no solo con metaheurísticas clásicas.
• A2 ↔ B2 (Multi-Agent Systems): comparten P21 — la gestión de demanda energética se aborda con sistemas multiagente.
• B1 ↔ B3 (LLM-Assisted RL): comparten P20 — los LLM empiezan a asistir al diseño de recompensas en RL para scheduling.
• B1 ↔ D1 (XAI): comparten P13 — la explicabilidad se está incorporando directamente a los agentes de RL, no solo a métodos clásicos.
• C1 (Digital Twin Frameworks) ↔ A1 y ↔ A2: comparten P26 y P27 — los gemelos digitales se apoyan tanto en modelos deterministas como en objetivos energéticos.
• C1 ↔ B1: comparte P30 — convergencia entre gemelos digitales y aprendizaje por refuerzo profundo.
• D1 ↔ D2 (Trust/Safety): comparten P6 — la transparencia técnica y la confianza organizacional se tratan juntas en la literatura de revisión.
Vacíos / zonas aisladas detectadas
C2 (IoT-Integrated Digital Twins) solo contiene un documento (P19) y no comparte ningún documento con otro subtema: es la rama más aislada del Document Set y una oportunidad clara para investigación futura o síntesis (relevante para la Tarea 3).

Task 3: Synthesis of Research Gaps and 
 Technological Frontiers 
 Document Analysis and Organizational Synthesis — 
 Industrial AI for Steel Production Scheduling 
 The knowledge map from Task 2 revealed a clear concentration of steelmaking 
 literature in deterministic and energy-efficiency models Cluster A, an 
 accelerated adoption of deep reinforcement learning Cluster B, and a marked 
 isolation of physical IoT integration within digital twins Subtopic C2. Based on 
 a cross-synthesis of all 31 articles in the Document Set, this document outlines 
 the identified research gaps, emerging technological frontiers, a future 
 research roadmap, and strategic recommendations for the steel industry.

Task 4: Integrative Synthesis
Document Analysis and Organizational Synthesis — Industrial AI for Steel Production Scheduling
Executive Summary & Unified Blueprint Vision
Task 3 identified significant domain isolations—most notably between physical IoT sensor infrastructures, prescriptive Digital Twins, Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) decision engines, and human-centric Explainable AI (XAI) interfaces. Task 4 re-converges these fragmented insights into an operational organizational strategy: the Cyber-Physical AI Steel Scheduling Framework (CPAI-SSF).
By grounding advanced DRL algorithms in real-time thermal physics provided by Digital Twins and validating AI actions through operator-centric XAI interfaces, CPAI-SSF bridges the gap between theoretical AI capabilities and strict metallurgical shop-floor constraints.

Delivery Performance: 15–20% reduction in job tardiness under dynamic perturbations [P3, P22].

4. Conclusion & Organizational Blueprint Summary
The Cyber-Physical AI Steel Scheduling Framework (CPAI-SSF) demonstrates that the future of steel manufacturing lies not in black-box automation, but in the tight integration of domain physics (Digital Twins), algorithmic agility (DRL), and human expertise (XAI / Industry 5.0). This unified blueprint turns theoretical advancements into a resilient, energy-efficient, and operational strategy for modern steelmaking.

Task 5: Final Report & Strategic Storytelling
Executive Briefing: Transforming Steel Production Scheduling via Cyber-Physical AI
Target Audience: Executive Board, Chief Operating Officer (COO), and Plant Directors
Strategic Focus: Transitioning from Fragmented Scheduling to an Integrated Cyber-Physical AI Architecture
1. ATTENTION — The Burning Platform: Energy Volatility and Bottleneck Losses
The Operational Crisis: Steel manufacturing faces unprecedented pressure from extreme electricity spot market price swings and escalating decarbonization targets. Thermal energy losses during buffer waiting times (e.g., ladle holding times and reheating furnace delays) account for severe operational margin leakage.
The Hidden Cost of Fragmented Systems: Current plant operations rely on siloed scheduling across production stages (ladles, reheating furnaces, and hot rolling mills). Partial sub-process optimization leads to downstream bottlenecks, heat degradation, and unplanned idle energy consumption.
The Imperative for Action: Maintaining legacy, static job-shop scheduling tools under today's market volatility guarantees compounding margin erosion and uncompetitive carbon intensity.
2. INTEREST — The Possibility of Change: Prescriptive Digital Twins & Deep RL
Algorithmic Agility (Deep Reinforcement Learning): Multi-agent Deep Q-Learning (DQL) agents evaluate thousands of rescheduling options per second. DRL dynamically aligns energy-intensive melting and reheating batches with low-tariff electricity windows and renewable generation availability.
Real-Time Thermal Physics (Live Digital Twins): By coupling physical IoT telemetry with prescriptive Digital Twin engines, plant managers gain live, predictive state estimation of steel temperature drops and equipment wear.
Proven Convergence: Literature syntheses across 31 industry benchmarks demonstrate that combining Digital Twins with DRL transforms passive monitoring into real-time prescriptive control, drastically reducing job tardiness and thermal holding losses.
3. DESIRE — The Security of the Approach: Industry 5.0 Governance & XAI
Eliminating 'Black-Box' Opacity: Operational teams often reject AI recommendations due to a lack of transparency. Our Cyber-Physical AI Steel Scheduling Framework (CPAI-SSF) integrates Explainable AI (XAI) layers that provide operators with real-time counterfactual logic (e.g., 'Reducing furnace speed by 5% reduces energy costs by 8% with zero impact on rolling mill throughput').
Operator Empowerment & Safety: CPAI-SSF acts as an Augmented Intelligence Assistant. Operators retain complete override authority and can interact with the scheduler using natural language prompts via Large Language Model (LLM) interfaces.
Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF): Veteran operator knowledge continuously tunes reward functions, ensuring that safety, quality, and human well-being are prioritized alongside mathematical efficiency.
4. ACTION — Implementation Roadmap & Concrete Next Steps
Projected Impact: Capturing an 8–12% reduction in reheating energy costs and a 15–20% reduction in job tardiness via a phased 24-month rollout.
